subject: Geopolitics
title: Farmland Grabs
description: A micro-lesson that makes Farmland Grabs usable.

hook.text: Saudi Arabia bought farmland in Ethiopia to grow food for Saudi citizens. Ethiopians on that land went hungry.

buildup.text: Land grabs occur when wealthy nations lease or buy farmland in poorer countries to secure their own food supply.

discovery.text: China, Gulf states, and India are the biggest buyers. Africa and Southeast Asia are the biggest sellers.

twist.text: The food grown is exported, not sold locally. Host nations lose land and gain almost nothing in return.

climax.text: As climate change shrinks arable land, farmland grabs will intensify. The next colonialism may be agricultural.

punchline.text: Buying another nation's soil is buying its sovereignty.

quiz.question: Why do wealthy nations buy farmland in poorer countries?
options: To help develop local agricultural technology
To secure their own food supply from foreign soil
To reduce carbon emissions from domestic farming
